title: Development and testing of a digital home assessment conference to optimise participation-oriented rehabilitation and provision of aids. A mixed-methods study.
summary:
The aim of the study is to develop a technical solution for virtual home conferences that is accepted by users.

In the first phase, a digital home conference will be created. This is intended to help assess the living situation of patients before discharge and advise them on the appropriate equipment and aids for their home. The conference will be implemented as an interactive virtual reality application with a video conferencing function. User groups are working on the technical development in workshops.

In the second phase, the application will be tested and evaluated in a clinic with spinal cord and neurorehabilitation patients. This involves analysing how well the technology is accepted, how satisfied users are with the application in everyday clinical practice and what benefits it brings for rehabilitation and aid counselling. The results will be recorded and analysed using interviews and questionnaires.
conditions: Cerebral palsy and other paralytic syndromes

interventions.name: At least one inpatient virtual home assessment with therapist and patient

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- impairments of the central and/or peripheral nervous system 
- the existing functional limitation(s) are likely to last longer and are associated with an increased risk of falling in the private home environment and/or require adaptations of the home environment to the patient's functional abilities
- unable to walk or only able to walk to a limited extent 
- discharge to home is planned
Exclusion criteria:
- Incapable of giving consent and legal guardianship not assumed by relatives
- Existence of conditions that preclude understanding of the intervention goal
